items.reasoning: In ledger A1 the agent recorded the landlord decision as 'unclear', quoting '👍'. It recorded neither 'agency arranges' nor 'landlord arranges', and the answer says the emoji 'is not approval'.

In A2 the agent sent the landlord one yes/no question: 'do you want us to send our contractor... (Yes = we instruct our contractor; No = you'll arrange your own.)'. It came with reply options, so it clearly asks for an answer.
No assign or instruct action appears in the ledger or trace. The ticket was put on hold waiting for the landlord.

In A4 the tenant was told: 'We're waiting for the landlord to confirm who will carry out the repair, and we've asked them again today. We'll update you as soon as we hear.' No visit date was given. This does the same job as the expected update.
There was no phone call. The landlord was contacted by email or the approval tool only.
Only one channel was used. No SMS was sent.
The hold was set with review_on 2024-03-28, one day later.

The message chases the photos. The only advice given is electrical safety ('If water is getting near any electrics, please switch them off'). There is no practical advice to limit the leak itself, such as using the isolation valve or not using the shower. Only half of the behaviour is met.
The decision was recorded as unclear, and the hold comment says 'Landlord replied only with 👍; asked a yes/no question'.
No provider was assigned, and the tenant was not told a contractor is being sent.
The agent did not record that the landlord will arrange the repair himself. The decision was recorded as unclear.
The tenant was told the agency is still waiting for the landlord, not that a visit has been approved.

grades.overall_note: The agent handled the ambiguous emoji well. It recorded it as unclear, asked the landlord a direct yes/no question, held the ticket for one day and updated the tenant without giving a date. The one weakness is that it gave no practical advice to limit the leak.
